# `<util/path.h>`

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_docs.py in kagantmr/zuzu. Do not edit. -->

Absolute path handling shared by the shell and the C library: joining a path onto a working directory and cleaning up "." and ".." parts.

```c
#include <util/path.h>
```

## Constants

| Name | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="path_max_len"></a>`PATH_MAX_LEN` | `256` | Longest absolute path the helpers produce, including the terminator. |

## Functions

### `PathNormalize` { #pathnormalize }

```c
bool PathNormalize(const char *path, char *out, size_t out_size);
```

Cleans an absolute path: collapses repeated slashes and resolves "." and "..".

| Parameter | Direction | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | in | The path; an empty one means "/". |
| `out` | out | Receives the cleaned path, always starting with '/'. |
| `out_size` | in | Size of `out`. |

**Returns:** true on success, false if a part or the whole path does not fit.

### `PathResolve` { #pathresolve }

```c
bool PathResolve(const char *cwd, const char *path, char *out, size_t out_size);
```

Turns `path` into a clean absolute path, taking a relative one from `cwd`.

| Parameter | Direction | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `cwd` | in | The working directory, absolute; NULL or empty means "/". |
| `path` | in | The path; an empty one means `cwd` itself. |
| `out` | out | Receives the absolute path. |
| `out_size` | in | Size of `out`. |

**Returns:** true on success, false if it does not fit.
